subject: botany_2
question_text: Mention the advantages of selecting pea plant for experiment by Mendel.

verification.note: Sourced from "Sr. Botany — My Baby Bullet-Q" (Sri Publishers, STAR-Q Pass Track), book p.30, printed question 31. Botany-II holds only ONE source book: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no Telangana Botany-II board paper is in the corpus, so the two-book union check and the board back-test are BOTH structurally impossible for this card — "not checked" does NOT mean "checked and clean". Run both the moment a second source or a real paper arrives. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Examiner audit revision (2026-09-05): the first s4_practical mistake demanded at least six reasons, a count the card's own four-row mark split does not support; it now asks for at least four, one for each mark.

insider_note: Seven reasons in the book, four marks on the paper. The two that must appear are the seven pairs of contrasting characters and the ability to self-pollinate.

page_header: Principles of Inheritance and Variation (Botany-II) · 4 marks

steps.label: Contrasting characters
steps.margin_note: Say contrasting, give the number seven, give one pair. This is the key reason.
lines: 1. The garden pea has MANY CONTRASTING
CHARACTERS, each with two clear alternatives.
Mendel used seven pairs: tall or dwarf, round or
wrinkled seed, green or yellow pod, and so on.
Each character is either one form or the other,
with nothing in between.
steps.why: A character with only two clear forms can be counted, and counting is what let Mendel turn breeding results into ratios.
common_mistakes: Saying pea has many characters. It has many CONTRASTING PAIRS, which is different.
Giving no example pair. Tall and dwarf is the standard one.
steps.memory_tip: Two clear forms means you can count, and counting gives ratios.

steps.label: Ease of crossing
steps.margin_note: Bisexual, self pollination, hand cross pollination. Three numbered points.
lines: 2. The pea flower is BISEXUAL: it has both male
and female parts in the same flower.
3. It can be SELF POLLINATED easily, which gives
pure breeding lines.
4. It can also be CROSS POLLINATED by hand,
which lets the experimenter choose the parents.
steps.why: Being able to both self and cross the same plant is what let Mendel make pure lines first and then cross them in a controlled way.
common_mistakes: Saying pea flowers are unisexual. They are BISEXUAL.
Giving only one of the two. Self AND cross pollination are both needed.
steps.memory_tip: Self it to make it pure, cross it to test it.

steps.label: Life cycle and progeny
steps.margin_note: Three more numbered points. The large-progeny point is the statistical one.
lines: 5. It has a SHORT LIFE CYCLE, so many
generations can be raised in a few years.
6. It produces a LARGE NUMBER of offspring, so
the ratios are reliable.
7. It has a SMALL NUMBER of chromosomes (7 pairs).
steps.why: A ratio measured on ten plants proves nothing; on thousands it becomes a law, so the number of offspring is as important as the plant's other qualities.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the large number of offspring. Big numbers are why the ratios held.
Saying pea has many chromosomes. It has SEVEN pairs, which is few.
steps.memory_tip: Quick, plentiful, and simple to follow.

steps.label: Practical advantages
steps.margin_note: Close with the practical points and one line joining them.

lines.text: Two clear forms, easy crosses, many offspring

lines: 8. It grows easily in ordinary garden conditions
and needs no special laboratory.
9. The characters are easy to see with the naked
eye, so no equipment is needed to score them.
Together these made pea the right plant for the
first experiments in heredity.
steps.why: Every advantage points the same way: the experiment could be run at scale, by one person, with nothing but a garden and careful records.
common_mistakes: Writing only one or two reasons. This is a list question carrying four marks, so give at least four reasons.
Naming an advantage without saying why it helped. The reason is what earns the mark.
steps.memory_tip: Anyone with a garden could have run it; only Mendel counted.
